newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian coal union says seeking dispute talks.
newsitem.headline: Australian coal union says seeking dispute talks.

text.p: The union representing striking coal miners at New South Wales' Hunter Valley Number One mine said on Wednesday it wants to start negotiations in the Industrial Relations Commission on Thursday.
The Construction Forestry Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) said all 412 of the striking miners have signed a petition urging Rio Tinto Ltd to recognise their right to be represented by the union.
The union intends to present the petition to Rio Tinto after a march through Sydney streets on Wednesday and demand an immediate start to talks.
CFMEU general president John Maitland said the union was prepared to negotiate even with individual contracts still on offer to workers, and with non-union labour working the mine.

"It's not a change of heart, it's really upping the ante as far as the company is concerned and seeing whether or not they are able to show any semblance of commitment to the workforce," Maitland told a news conference.
The five-week old strike centres on Rio Tinto's bid to offer individual workplace agreements to all staff at the mine, which is operated by 71 percent owned subsidiry Coal & Allied.
Coal & Allied has estimated each day of the strike is costing the company about A$1 million in lost revenue.
